title: pm-dispatch: group work by mechanism — security advisories and area cards get one analysis and one combined fix PR per group
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

Filing gate ③: maintainer-directed task. Ruling-ref: the maintainer said 「按机制归组，每组做一次分析、出一个合并修复 PR, 同意，立卡修改skills」 (2026-11-19, seat 5 thread), answering seat 5's cost proposal for security fixes. ⛔ Not a claim. Sibling of #35270 (effort policy); the two may land in one PR. Not part of epic #35205; overlap-check its open step PRs first (same files). This card names no advisory, count or mechanism, and the PR ⛔ must not either.

## Why

The security lane today handles advisories one at a time: one read, one analysis note, one fix dispatch at `xhigh`, one PR, one L2 review each (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/security.md:17-28`, `security-findings.md:27`). Many open advisories share a root mechanism, so the same analysis and the same fix shape are paid for again per advisory.

## What to do

Edit `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/security.md` and the matching lines of `references/security-findings.md` (re-read line numbers on main):

1. **Group before fixing.** On intake and on each patrol, the security seat sorts every `draft` advisory into a group by shared root mechanism (same missing check, same door family, same owning package). A group has one lead advisory. An advisory that shares nothing is a group of one.
2. **One analysis per group.** The seat writes one analysis for the group and appends it to the lead advisory via relay `advisory_note`; every other advisory in the group gets a one-line note pointing at the lead. Mechanism stays only in advisories and the dispatch order, as today.
3. **One combined fix PR per group.** One no-card dispatch order per group, one branch, one PR, one L2 review. A group never spans two owning packages' release lines, and a PR stays inside the normal size limits; a group too large splits into ordered PRs. Each advisory in the group gets its own regression test that reproduces its attack (fails before the fix, passes after), so the PR proves every member, not just the lead.
4. **Ledger.** The seat post's ledger row gains an opaque group tag (`G1`, `G2`, …), never a mechanism word. Every member moves `fixing` → `merged` → `closed` together when the group PR merges.
5. **Order.** Groups holding a high- or medium-severity advisory go first. Low-severity advisories are fixed only inside such a group (riding it), not on their own, in line with the maintainer's p1/p2-only dispatch rule.
6. **Effort** follows #35270 (high-severity: `high` build plus an `xhigh` read-only diff review; medium: `high`; grouping and analysis at `high`). Replace the flat `xhigh` at `security-findings.md:27` accordingly.
7. **Publishing list** (`security.md:35`) lists by group, members under their lead, high and medium first.

## Same idea for ordinary areas (maintainer asked 「其他 area 可以用类似的方案吗？」, seat 5 proposal)

Edit `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md` (and the triage filing line it points at):

8. **Triage tags the mechanism.** When filing or triaging, a card whose root cause matches an open card's gets a `Same-mechanism: #N` line naming the lead card.
9. **Areas fold at claim time.** An area claiming a card folds its open same-mechanism or same-file p1/p2 siblings in its lease into one claim, one `os-dev` order, one PR and one review (the existing fold, made the default): at most 5 cards, one owning package, normal size limits; a p3 may ride under the existing rule.
10. **One analysis per fold.** Where a card needs a design or maintainer decision, the analysis covers the whole fold and the decision is asked once.

## Done when

The lane and area text say the above, the public lane file still names no finding, count, path or mechanism, the skill gates pass, and the PR carries a contract review (governed `.claude/**`). Seat 5 reviews and lands.
